days.studyBrief: Complete algebra/function gaps; prioritise discriminants, factor/remainder theorem, simultaneous equations and inequalities.
days.dailyTarget: Close specification gaps; ≥85% after review
days.notes: Accuracy first; look for structural shortcuts.

days.studyBrief: Sequences/series, recurrences, lines, circles and intersections.
days.dailyTarget: Close specification gaps; ≥85% after review
days.notes: Write one-line recognition notes after each miss.

days.studyBrief: Exact values, radians, trig graphs/equations, sine/cosine rules and 2D/3D reasoning.
days.dailyTarget: Close specification gaps; ≥85% after review
days.notes: No calculator; sketch before solving.

days.studyBrief: Recall graph features, then practise transformations, asymptotes, intercepts, range and sketching. Finish by correcting graph-related errors.
days.dailyTarget: Sketch from structure, not appearance.
days.notes: Review: mark methods, record the initiating idea, and flag any graph still based on guessing.

days.studyBrief: Repair signed-area interpretation and practise compact graph/calculus recognition rather than a broad calculus syllabus.
days.dailyTarget: Explain the geometry before integrating.
days.notes: Tuesday work starts after 14:00. Review signs, regions, tangent/curve order and faster recognition.

days.studyBrief: Build reliable probability, counting and data foundations, then finish with a short SMC efficiency set.
days.dailyTarget: Use systematic cases and state the sample space.
days.notes: The SMC block is deliberately short: spotting and economy, not a second syllabus.

days.studyBrief: Sit the Euclid R2DREW2 Paper 1 under timed conditions, then complete a structured error and timing analysis.
days.dailyTarget: Complete one representative Paper 1 and analyse every loss.
days.notes: Use the local verified-page mark scheme. Do not create a result until the paper is actually attempted.

days.studyBrief: Practise implication, converse, contrapositive, necessary/sufficient conditions and counterexamples with explanation-first work.
days.dailyTarget: State the logical form before calculating.
days.notes: Prioritise understanding and counterexamples over volume.

days.studyBrief: Think aloud through a small set of unfamiliar CSAT, STEP I and MAT problems. Explain decomposition, failed approaches and adaptation.
days.dailyTarget: Explain the approach aloud before finalising it.
days.notes: Tuesday work starts after 14:00. This is deliberately not another TMUA multiple-choice session.

days.studyBrief: Target circles, coordinates and efficient geometry alongside exact values, radians/degrees, periods and transformed trig graphs.
days.dailyTarget: Use exact structure before numerical or visual guessing.
days.notes: Review the known coordinate-geometry and trig errors explicitly.

days.studyBrief: Sit the Euclid Sample Paper 2 under timed conditions, then analyse logical form, approach choice and time use.
days.dailyTarget: Complete one representative Paper 2 and explain each error.
days.notes: Use the local verified-page mark scheme; this is diagnostic, not an extreme challenge paper.

days.studyBrief: Practise ratio, scaling, bounds and number structure, then use a short SMC observation set for speed.
days.dailyTarget: Look for structure before expanding arithmetic.
days.notes: Retain useful ratio work while keeping the SMC segment modest.

days.studyBrief: Connect functions, transformations, sequences and recurrences, then solve two deeper CSAT-style problems with written reflection.
days.dailyTarget: Name the structure and recurrence before manipulating it.
days.notes: Tuesday work starts after 14:00; finish by explaining one unfamiliar problem aloud.

days.studyBrief: Consolidate counting, conditional probability and data interpretation, ending with a timed mixed section.
days.dailyTarget: Make cases exhaustive and avoid hidden double-counting.
days.notes: Mechanics is intentionally omitted because it is not the current repair priority.

days.studyBrief: Sit the complete official 2017 Paper 1 under exam conditions, then review topic, timing and approach errors.
days.dailyTarget: Complete and fully review the official Paper 1 benchmark.
days.notes: Assignments are created now; attempts and results are recorded only when the paper is actually done.

days.studyBrief: Sit the complete official 2017 Paper 2 under exam conditions and give logic/approach errors a full review.
days.dailyTarget: Complete and fully review the official Paper 2 benchmark.
days.notes: Paper 2 receives deliberate early benchmark exposure because it is the relative weakness.

days.studyBrief: Use the current Needs Review/Redo set and known graph, trig, probability and approach weaknesses as the deterministic repair seed.
days.dailyTarget: Redo without looking, then write the initiating idea.
days.notes: Later benchmark-driven repair requires a plan refresh; this migration does not fabricate future performance.

days.studyBrief: Think aloud through a small Cambridge-focused mix. State assumptions, react to hints, explain failed routes and summarise each argument.
days.dailyTarget: Prioritise explanation and adaptation over question count.
days.notes: Tuesday work starts after 14:00. BMO is limited to one suitable problem.

days.studyBrief: Sit official 2018 Paper 1 under timed conditions and complete substantial method, error and timing review.
days.dailyTarget: Complete and review the official Paper 1 benchmark.
days.notes: No fake attempts or results are created by migration.

days.studyBrief: Sit official 2018 Paper 2 under timed conditions and complete substantial logic, error and timing review.
days.dailyTarget: Complete and review the official Paper 2 benchmark.
days.notes: No fake attempts or results are created by migration.

days.studyBrief: Run both official 2019 papers in exam conditions with a proper break, then capture post-simulation notes and begin analysis.
days.dailyTarget: Complete both papers; preserve exam conditions and the break.
days.notes: This is an intentionally exceptional long day. Analysis may continue on Day 22.

days.studyBrief: Analyse the 2019 simulation first, repair recurring topic/time/approach errors, then add only a light CSAT reasoning block.
days.dailyTarget: Turn each recurring error into a concrete rule or repair action.
days.notes: Tuesday work starts after 14:00. Paper analysis takes priority over the light CSAT block.

days.studyBrief: Use a coherent hard JZ/Challenge Paper 2 set for logic, counterexamples, subtle structure and pressure handling.
days.dailyTarget: Stay precise under stretch difficulty; stop and analyse rather than grind.
days.notes: This is a selected hard set, not a wholesale challenge bank.

days.studyBrief: Combine a short SMC speed set, two deeper BMO problems and two unfamiliar CSAT problems for controlled mathematical flexibility.
days.dailyTarget: Solve efficiently, then explain the deeper arguments clearly.
days.notes: TMUA remains the priority; the crossover workload is deliberately bounded.

days.studyBrief: Sit official 2020 Paper 1 under timed conditions and complete substantial review.
days.dailyTarget: Complete and review the official Paper 1 benchmark.
days.notes: The paper remains unavailable to automatic practice before today.

days.studyBrief: Sit official 2020 Paper 2 under timed conditions and complete substantial review.
days.dailyTarget: Complete and review the official Paper 2 benchmark.
days.notes: Tuesday work starts after 14:00; the paper remains protected before today.

days.studyBrief: Repair recurring error classes and practise question selection, abandonment/return decisions, exact values and fast structural recognition.
days.dailyTarget: Choose a method quickly and define when to move on.
days.notes: No large fresh paper: this is controlled efficiency and repair work.

days.studyBrief: Run both official 2021 papers as the final exhausting simulation, with a proper break and planned analysis.
days.dailyTarget: Complete the final two-paper simulation under exam conditions.
days.notes: This is the last major full simulation; no result is created until the work is actually done.

days.studyBrief: Use the strongest current evidence—error notes, Needs Review/Redo and recurring weak topics—for a small final repair set.
days.dailyTarget: Resolve remaining repeatable errors; do not chase novelty.
days.notes: Later benchmark data can replace priorities through a future explicit plan refresh.

days.studyBrief: Use a very small seen-question set alongside logic forms, exact trig, graph, probability, algebra and timing reminders.
days.dailyTarget: Finish the personal error log and exam decision rules.
days.notes: No exhausting new material. Thursday is rest; Friday is the stored exam date.
